purpose: Two questions this batch answers that the source evidence cannot: (1) do these eight dispositions reproduce on the newest candidate, or were any of them candidate-specific; (2) does the tool-call waste observed in the source run (shell pipelines passed as literal args, command name repeated as args[0]) recur on the newest tool surface. It is a variance check, not a capability measurement: the source run's verdicts stand unchanged and this batch's own numbers are never published as a rate.

admission.rule: AGENTS.md:11 — a declared re-measurement is the only way an already-graded cell may be measured again, and it never replaces the verdict it re-measures. All eight cells already carry a canonical verdict (seven from run 39557190033, meriyah from its recovery run 39585210102). Each receives exactly one extra attempt, admitted under the variance-check class, with the frozen per-cell official budget, the same grader and the same generation parallelism as the source run. No cell receives a second extra attempt in this manifest.
admission.class: variance check — the source verdict stands and is not replaced; this attempt asks whether the same frozen composition reproduces the same terminal state on a newer candidate

constraints: One predeclared headless attempt per cell; no cell receives a second extra attempt in this manifest.

knownRisks.providerTransport: The source run recorded six transport stalls across these cells for 2246 seconds. A recurrence costs a cell its verdict exactly as measured and is disclosed, never retried.
knownRisks.noFixesIncluded: This candidate carries none of the tool-contract fixes in docs/benchmarks/tool-contract-disposition-list.md. A comparison against a later fixed candidate must therefore be read as candidate-plus-fix, not as the fix alone.
knownRisks.budget: Each cell keeps the official budget the source run declared; none is extended.
knownRisks.finality: One attempt per cell. A cell that dies again keeps no new verdict and its source verdict still stands.
